newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sampoerna falls on Moody's news.
newsitem.headline: Sampoerna falls on Moody's news.

text.p: Shares in Indonesian cigarette maker PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna fell sharply on Monday after news that Moody's had placed $200 million in notes issued by a subsidiary on review for a possible downgrade, brokers said.
The share fell 1,050 rupiah to 21,400 by 0310 GMT.

Brokers said the news of the possible downgrade came as Sampoerna announced it had secured a fresh short-term bank facility of $400 million, and they were confused about why the company was seeking fresh funds.
On Saturday, the company announced it had obtained a new $400 million loan but the terms were not disclosed. It said the money would be used for corporate development.

"Corporate development includes a number of aims such as ongoing expansion in domestic and overseas markets, to finance our inventory and also for acquisitions," said company spokesman Jonathan Zax on Monday. He declined to elaborate.

Mooday's said it had placed the Baa3 rating of Sampoerna International Finance Co B.V.'s $200 million notes on review following acquisitions made by a company subsidiary and president director Putera Sampoerna in car-maker Astra International.

Moody's said the moves "clearly indicate that Sampoerna intends to pursue a much more aggressive diversification strategy away from its original plan as well as its willingness to use a higher level of debt capacity for this purpose".

Moody's said the review would focus on the prospects for further investment by Sampoerna in Astra and, if the investment materialised, the method of financing, its impact on the predictability of the company's overall cash flow, and the magnitude of additional business and political risk incurred.
